# Matroska Dolby packet clock controls

The first five controls wrap the first four E-AC-3 syncframes of the
repository's [synthetic mixed fixture](../mkv-feed/README.md) in an authored
Matroska Segment. Each uses a 1 ms timestamp scale, no DefaultDuration, a
single audio track and one Cluster at zero. SimpleBlocks use Xiph lacing
where two frames share a timestamp. The damaged control flips the last
bit of its first syncframe to exercise duration backfill.

| Control | Block offsets in ms and frame indices |
|---|---|
| `laced-unknown-duration` | 0 (1, 2), 96 (3, 4) |
| `initial-negative-cluster-relative` | −32 (1), 0 (2), 64 (3) |
| `two-laced-before-first-known-pts` | −64 (1, 2), 96 (3, 4) |
| `no-absolute-anchor` | −128 (1), −96 (2) |
| `damaged-lace-before-valid-anchor` | −64 (damaged 1, 2), 96 (3, 4) |

The sixth control, `laced-fractional-cadence`, uses eight silent 44.1 kHz
syncframes generated by FFmpeg 9.0.2. It places Xiph laces at −80 ms
(frames 1–2), 120 ms (3–6) and −300 ms (7–8). The reference publishes and
advances by 34 whole ticks per frame.

```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i anullsrc=r=44100:cl=stereo -frames:a 8 \
  -c:a eac3 -b:a 96k -f eac3 44100.eac3
```

The expected PTS, DTS and durations in the Rust test come from FFprobe
revision `d32b387f2b0a484599d4587d651891f0c63c4238`.
The macOS ARM64 reference executable SHA-256 was
`98f423c6f7050c7f44927d1660568a313a926c5c4d14e98ef6fec9117039a230`.

```sh
ffprobe -v error -select_streams a -show_packets \
  -show_entries packet=pts,dts,duration -of csv=p=0 path/to/control.mkv
```
